artifact: Phase 8 GRC/LGRC I111 raw-domain demand interpretation execution
interpretation_boundary: Expert-authored demand-to-substrate decomposition is visible and auditable; this is not automatic natural-language selection.

raw_rows.consumer_language: I already know the source, receiver, amount, and delay. I only need the amount to leave, remain in flight, and arrive without creating a second composition.
raw_rows.normalization_reason: The demand supplies route, amount, and time and requires no crossing beyond packet transport.
claim_ceiling: native packet accounting and queue-processing mechanics

raw_rows.consumer_language: A participant is depleted while nearby regions have excess capacity. I want current state to form possible receivers and decide a viable continuation without supplying a fixed target.
raw_rows.normalization: state-conditioned surplus should form candidate receivers before native arbitration
raw_rows.normalization_reason: The representative matrix contains no surplus-to-candidate-formation crossing; absence is not a missing-crossing finding.
raw_rows.claim_ceiling: No composition or missing-crossing claim; the directional pair requires source audit and registration if retained.
raw_rows.next_action: source audit and new registration if the demand remains important

raw_rows.consumer_language: Several routes look possible. I want current sink compatibility to determine which route becomes scheduled rather than supplying the route myself.
raw_rows.normalization: sink compatibility should author an event-time route schedule
raw_rows.normalization_reason: The registered sink-choice-to-route-schedule crossing is explicitly absent.
claim_ceiling: Unsupported until an explicit admission and scheduling relation is supplied.
raw_rows.missing_relation: LGRC runtime has no consumer of GRC9V3 choice_registry or collapse_registry

raw_rows.consumer_language: A trace from earlier packet activity survives replay. I need to know whether persistence alone means later native behavior reads that trace.
raw_rows.normalization: persisted ledger history should become a constitutive later read
raw_rows.normalization_reason: Restoration retains ledger state but no native constitutive consumer reads it.
claim_ceiling: Ledger persistence and replay identity only.
raw_rows.missing_relation: restoration preserves packet ledger but no native constitutive consumer reads ledger history to alter later eligibility or geometry

raw_rows.consumer_language: One participant changes a non-private trace and a later encounter with that trace should change whether another packet is scheduled.
raw_rows.normalization: packet arrival records a surface, lineage is read by a producer, and producer eligibility schedules a later packet
raw_rows.normalization_reason: Surface emission is native/configured, while both read-back eligibility and later scheduling remain producer-owned.
claim_ceiling: Producer-mediated feedback eligibility followed by native packet mechanics.

raw_rows.consumer_language: Local outward pressure at a capacity-bearing boundary should create and fund a child topology without treating birth eligibility as generic exchange admission.
raw_rows.normalization: outward flux and configured front capacity admit topology-specific boundary birth
raw_rows.normalization_reason: The native/configured birth crossing is registered and remains topology-specific.

raw_rows.consumer_language: After a topology commit I want child-basin and flow-window records, but I need to know whether those records caused the basin or only describe it.
raw_rows.normalization: post-commit topology is projected into child-basin diagnostics
raw_rows.normalization_reason: The records follow the commit and do not own topology mutation.
claim_ceiling: Diagnostic records over a committed native/configured topology event.
